sections.content:
6,635 people

were counted on the census as "steel erectors" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Steel erectors fit and put up structural metal framework for buildings and other structures such as metal chimneys.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "steel erectors" there were more men than women (99.1% compared with 0.9%).

This means "steel erectors" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled construction and building trades".

Men made up 99.1% and women made up 0.9% of "steel erectors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "steel erectors" included:

  • pipe fitters
  • plasterers
  • bricklayers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "steel erectors" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "steel erectors", 14.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "steel erectors" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "steel erectors" included:

  • electrical engineers
  • water and sewerage plant operatives
  • stock control clerks and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "steel erectors", 6.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.7% compared with 6.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (55.4%) than self-employed (44.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was Yorkshire and the Humber. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Shropshire, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
